survey: Image 5 is a round analog clock. It has a thick, glossy orange ring around a white dial. The dial has 12 dark-blue hour bars with small minute dots between them. Two dark-blue hands (hour and minute) and a thin red second hand meet at a single dark-blue center cap. The clock faces the camera, turned slightly to the right, and stands upright on the bottom curve of its ring on a green floor, with a soft shadow under it. The ring is round, allowing for perspective, and the dial is centered in it. All three hands share one pivot. The hands show about 10:09: the hour hand sits just past the 10, which agrees with the minute hand at about 9 minutes. Each hand has a sensible length, and there are no extra or missing hour bars. The only weak point is support: there is no stand, foot or back leg. A round body balanced on one point of its rim would roll or tip over.

errors.where: Bottom of the orange ring, where the clock touches the floor
errors.what: The round clock stands upright on its curved rim with no stand, feet or back prop. A disc resting on a single point could not stay upright and would roll or fall over.

fix: Give the round orange clock a small stand: two short orange feet at the bottom of the ring, or a slanted prop leg at the back, so it sits steadily on the floor instead of balancing on its curved rim.
